page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance delivering direct access to host hardware resources. Powered by Intel Xeon 8124M processors running at 3.4 GHz across an x86_64 architecture, the platform exposes 36 physical cores and 72 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 192 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. L3 cache measures 24 MB alongside 1 MB L2 cache per core. As a dedicated metal offering, virtualization overhead is eliminated, enabling direct execution of low-level instructions including AVX-512 and hardware virtualization primitives.

Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included, and the instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage, relying entirely on remote elastic block storage. However, c5n.metal integrates high-capacity network connectivity with a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate top-quartile performance across highly parallelized CPU and memory workflows. Multi-core stress-ng throughput ranks in the top 25%, matched by strong PassMark CPU scores, PassMark extended instruction evaluations, and high-throughput Clang software compilation. Read-only memory bandwidth reaches 212.97 GB/sec for large uncached blocks and over 3,741 GB/sec for cached blocks. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core remain in the average tier.

Because of its lack of dedicated GPU hardware, text generation throughput on small and medium large language models places in the bottom decile. Cost efficiency is characterized by dense multi-threaded x86 compute and substantial 100 Gbps interconnect capacity rather than local I/O density. Consequently, AWS c5n.metal is structured for network-intensive compute clusters, distributed CI/CD build farms, batch processing, scientific simulations requiring AVX-512 routines, and high-packet networking middleboxes.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server engineered for high-throughput parallel execution and intensive networking. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz, it provides 36 physical cores, 72 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture, and 192 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The instance features no local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, requiring attached network volumes for persistence. A prominent differentiator is its baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, c5n.metal achieves top-quartile scores in multi-core CPU testing, software compilation, and uncached read memory bandwidth, while single-core compute and LLM text generation exhibit lower relative output. Without hypervisor latency, c5n.metal delivers predictable performance and qualitative resource efficiency for parallel computational tasks, distributed network proxies, clustered simulations, and automated continuous integration pipelines.
